The conceptual stack frame contains:
1. the arguments of the procedure
2. place to hold local variables
3. magic information to be able to return from a call

Implementation of stack:
The CPU can be described by:
the instruction pointer (IP): a reference to the next instruction to execute
a stack pointer (SP): a reference to the top of the stack
a base pointer (BP): a reference to the current stack frame
general purpose registers: used by a process to store data

Data structures placed on the stack will not be available once we return from a call.
The space required to store the structures can be reused immediately.
Not all data structures could be allocated on the stack (not the ones that should live for longer).
Data structures that should survive a return should be placed on the heap.

If you forget to do free, you will have a memory leak.
If you do free twice, undefined behavior.
If you access a structure after free, undefined behavior.
